title: Choosing a Journal, Spotting Predatory Journals and Answering Reviewers

hook.en: You finished the paper. Now an email arrives: "We will publish your article in 48 hours for a small fee." Tempting, and a trap. Where you publish decides whether anyone trusts, finds and cites your work. Learn to choose well, and to handle peer review without taking it personally.
hook.ur: Aap ka paper mukammal ho gaya. Ab ek email aati hai: "Hum aap ka article 48 ghanton mein chhap denge, thori si fees par." Lubhane wali baat hai, aur jaal bhi. Aap kahan chhapte hain yeh tay karta hai ke koi aap ke kaam par bharosa karega, dhoondhe ga aur hawala dega ya nahi. Achha chunna seekhein, aur peer review ko zaati liye baghair sambhalna.

goal.en: By the end, you'll shortlist suitable journals, check a journal with a simple checklist, recognise predatory journals and fake invitations, understand how peer review works, and write a calm point-by-point reply to reviewers.
goal.ur: End tak aap munasib journals ki fehrist banayenge, saade checklist se journal jaanchenge, predatory journals aur jhoote dawat-name pehchanenge, peer review ka amal samjhenge, aur reviewers ko pur-sukoon point-by-point jawab likhenge.

text.en: A good journal fits your topic and readers, is **indexed** in trusted databases, has a clear **peer review** process and transparent fees, and is run by a real editorial board. **Peer review** means independent experts judge your paper before it is published. A **predatory journal** takes fees but offers little or no real review, misleads about indexing or impact, and may publish almost anything. Many new authors are targeted by emails promising quick publication.
text.ur: Achha journal aap ke mauzu aur parhne walon se milta hai, bharosemand databases mein **index** hota hai, saaf **peer review** ka amal aur shaffaf fees rakhta hai, aur asal editorial board chalata hai. **Peer review** ka matlab hai ke azaad maahireen paper chhapne se pehle usay parkhte hain. **Predatory journal** fees leta hai lekin asal review kam ya bilkul nahi deta, indexing ya impact ke baare mein gumrah karta hai, aur lagbhag kuch bhi chhap sakta hai. Bohat se naye musannifon ko jaldi chhapne ke wade wali emails se nishana banaya jata hai.

text.en: Think of **a hospital**. A good hospital has qualified doctors, a licence, clear charges and a record of results. A fake clinic has a big signboard and a smiling receptionist, and takes your money. Before you hand over your paper, check the "licence": who runs it, who indexes it and who has published there.
text.ur: **Aspatal** sochein. Achhe aspatal mein qabil doctors, licence, saaf kharch aur nateejon ka record hota hai. Jhoote clinic ka bara signboard aur muskurati receptionist hoti hai, aur woh aap ka paisa le leta hai. Paper dene se pehle "licence" jaanchein: kaun chalata hai, kaun index karta hai aur wahan kis ne chhapa hai.

title.en: A five-minute check before you submit
title.ur: Bhejne se pehle paanch minute ki jaanch

steps.title: Does it fit?
steps.detail: Read its aims and a few recent papers. Is your topic, design and audience a natural fit? A mismatch is the most common reason for quick rejection. || Kya fit hai?

steps.title: Is it indexed where it says it is?
steps.detail: Search the journal in PubMed, Scopus or the Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ), and do not trust a logo on its own website. Check your country's recognition list too (for example, HEC in Pakistan, whose rules change, so use the current list). || Kya woh wahin index hai jahan kehta hai?

steps.title: Is the process and the cost clear?
steps.detail: A real journal states its peer review process, typical timelines, article charges and who the editors are. Hidden fees that appear after acceptance are a red flag. || Kya amal aur kharch saaf hain?

steps.title: Ask people and use a checklist
steps.detail: Ask your supervisor or librarian, and use the Think. Check. Submit. checklist. Search whether the journal's name appears in lists of problem journals. || Logon se poochhein aur checklist istemal karein

question.en: An email says: "Your recent thesis impressed us. Publish in our journal in 3 days with guaranteed acceptance." What is the best response?
question.ur: Email kehti hai: "Aap ki haal ki thesis ne mutasir kiya. Hamare journal mein 3 din mein chhapein, qabooliyat ki zamanat ke saath." Behtareen jawab kya hai?

text.en: Send the full paper and pay to see what happens
text.ur: Poora paper bhej dein aur dekhne ke liye paisa dein

feedback.en: Money first is a warning sign.
feedback.ur: Pehle paisa khatre ki nishani hai.

text.en: Treat it as a likely predatory approach: do not reply, and check the journal independently before considering it
text.ur: Isay mumkina predatory rabta samjhein: jawab na dein, aur sochne se pehle journal ko azaad taur par jaanchein

feedback.en: Yes — guaranteed acceptance and speed with no review are classic warning signs.
feedback.ur: Haan — qabooliyat ki zamanat aur review ke baghair raftar aam khabardar karne wali nishaniyan hain.

text.en: Accept at once because it is fast and flattering
text.ur: Foran qabool karein kyunke jaldi aur khushamad hai

feedback.en: Speed and flattery are the bait.

question.en: A journal's website shows a "Scopus indexed" badge, but you cannot find the journal in Scopus. What does this mean?
question.ur: Journal ki website par "Scopus indexed" ka badge hai, lekin aap Scopus mein journal dhoondh nahi paate. Is ka kya matlab hai?

text.en: The journal is brand new, which is fine
text.ur: Journal bilkul naya hai, jo theek hai

feedback.en: A false claim is not just newness.

text.en: The claim may be false; verify indexing yourself in the database, not on the journal's own website
text.ur: Daawa jhoota ho sakta hai; indexing database mein khud jaanchein, journal ki apni website par nahi

feedback.en: Yes — misleading indexing claims are a common sign of a predatory journal.
feedback.ur: Haan — gumrah karne wale indexing ke daawe predatory journal ki aam nishani hain.

question.en: A reviewer says your sample is too small and asks for more analyses. Which reply is best?
question.ur: Reviewer kehta hai aap ka sample bohat chhota hai aur mazeed tajziye maangta hai. Behtareen jawab kaun sa hai?

text.en: Argue that the reviewer does not understand your study
text.ur: Bahas karein ke reviewer aap ka study nahi samjha

feedback.en: Defensive replies often lead to rejection.
feedback.ur: Difa'i jawab aksar radd hone tak le jate hain.

text.en: Thank them, agree the limitation, add it to the limitations paragraph, run the extra analyses if sensible or explain politely why not, and show the change in the paper
text.ur: Un ka shukriya, had se ittefaq karein, hadon ke paragraph mein jorein, munasib ho to mazeed tajziye karein ya shaistagi se batayein kyun nahi, aur paper mein tabdeeli dikhayein

feedback.en: Yes — a calm, point-by-point answer wins editors' trust.
feedback.ur: Haan — pur-sukoon, point-by-point jawab editors ka bharosa jeet-ta hai.

text.ur: Comment nazar-andaaz kar ke dobara bhej dein

text.en: **Submitting to the first journal that says yes, or taking rejection personally.** Most good papers are rejected at least once. A rejection with comments is free advice. Also, do not submit one paper to several journals at once, and do not ignore a reviewer's point: either change the paper or explain, politely, why you did not. Never pay a fee before acceptance to a journal you have not checked.
text.ur: **Pehle haan kehne wale journal ko bhej dena, ya radd hone ko zaati lena.** Zyada tar achhe papers kam az kam ek baar radd hote hain. Comments ke saath radd hona muft mashwara hai. Ek paper ek saath kai journals ko na bhejein, aur reviewer ke kisi nukte ko nazar-andaaz na karein: ya paper badlein ya shaistagi se batayein kyun nahi. Jo journal aap ne jaancha nahi usay qabool hone se pehle kabhi fees na dein.

text.en: **Make a one-page "response to reviewers" table.** Copy each comment, write your reply and say exactly where in the paper the change is (page and line). Begin with a thank-you, keep a calm tone and do not argue. Editors read these tables carefully, and a clear one often turns "revise" into "accept".
text.ur: **"Reviewers ko jawab" ki ek safha ki table banayein.** Har comment copy karein, apna jawab likhein aur batayein paper mein tabdeeli theek kahan hai (safha aur line). Shukriya se shuru karein, pur-sukoon lehja rakhein aur bahas na karein. Editors yeh tables ghaur se parhte hain, aur saaf table aksar "revise" ko "accept" mein badal deti hai.

question.ur: Kya "open access" aur "predatory" ek hi cheez hain?

answer.en: No. Open access means anyone can read the paper free, and many excellent journals are open access, charging fees to authors to cover costs. Predatory describes the quality and honesty of the process, not whether access is free. Some subscription journals are poor too. Judge the journal by its review, indexing, transparency and track record, not by its business model alone.
answer.ur: Nahi. Open access ka matlab hai ke koi bhi paper muft parh sakta hai, aur bohat se shandar journals open access hain, jo kharch poora karne ke liye musannifon se fees lete hain. Predatory amal ki quality aur imaandari ko batata hai, yeh nahi ke rasai muft hai. Kuch subscription journals bhi kamzor hote hain. Journal ko uske review, indexing, shaffafiyat aur record se parkhein, sirf business model se nahi.

beats.patient: A final-year student receives an invitation from "International Journal of Advanced Physio Science" promising a decision in 5 days for 300 US dollars. The editor's page lists no names, the address is a post box, and the website claims "impact factor 8.2" without a source.
beats.assessment: Several red flags: unnamed editors, fast guaranteed decision, vague address, an unverified impact claim and fees up front.
beats.treatment: She searches the journal in DOAJ and Scopus (not found), asks her supervisor, and instead picks a physiotherapy journal that her supervisor has used, indexed in PubMed with a clear review process.
beats.reassess: Her paper is rejected once, revised after the reviewers' comments and then accepted, and the process improves it.

text.en: **Protect your work and your patients.** A paper in a journal with no real review may carry errors that readers trust and act on. Never publish clinical advice you would not defend to a patient. Do not submit identifiable patient details, and check that ethics approval, consent and trial registration are stated, as honest journals require.
text.ur: **Apne kaam aur mareezon ko mehfooz rakhein.** Jis journal mein asal review na ho wahan chhapa paper ghaltiyan rakh sakta hai jin par parhne wale bharosa kar ke amal karein. Aisa clinical mashwara kabhi na chhapein jis ka aap mareez ke saamne difa na kar saken. Mareez ki pehchan wali tafseelat na bhejein, aur dekhein ke ethics ki manzoori, razamandi aur trial registration likhi hain, jaisa imaandar journals taqaza karte hain.

text.en: Grudniewicz and colleagues, after a consensus process, defined predatory journals and publishers as entities that prioritise self-interest at the expense of scholarship, characterised by false or misleading information, deviation from best editorial and publication practices, a lack of transparency and aggressive, indiscriminate solicitation. Shamseer and colleagues compared potential predatory and legitimate biomedical journals and found that predatory journals more often had unclear or hidden fees, unusual or missing peer review details, false indexing claims and misleading metrics, although the two groups overlapped.
text.ur: Grudniewicz aur saathiyon ne ittefaq-e-raye ke baad predatory journals aur publishers ki tareef ki ke woh aise idare hain jo ilm ke nuqsan par apne mufaad ko tarjeeh dete hain, jin ki pehchan jhoothi ya gumrah karne wali maloomat, behtareen editorial aur isha'at amal se inhiraf, shaffafiyat ki kami aur jarahat pasand, be-tamiz dawat hai. Shamseer aur saathiyon ne mumkina predatory aur jaiz biomedical journals ka muqabla kiya aur paya ke predatory journals mein ghair wazeh ya chhupi fees, ghair mamooli ya ghayab peer review ki tafseel, jhoote indexing ke daawe aur gumrah karne wali metrics zyada thin, halaanke dono groups kuch had tak ek doosre se milte thay.

text.en: **Fit, Index, Process, Ask.** Does it fit, is it really indexed, is the process and cost clear, and have you asked someone?
text.ur: **Fit, Index, Process, Poochhein.** Kya fit hai, kya sach mein index hai, kya amal aur kharch saaf hain, aur kya kisi se poochha?

summary.en: Choose a journal that fits, is truly indexed, and has a clear peer review process and costs.
summary.ur: Aisa journal chunein jo fit ho, sach mein index ho, aur saaf peer review aur kharch rakhta ho.

summary.en: Predatory journals promise speed and guaranteed acceptance, mislead about indexing, and take fees without real review.
summary.ur: Predatory journals raftar aur qabooliyat ki zamanat ka waada karte hain, indexing ke baare mein gumrah karte hain, aur asal review ke baghair fees lete hain.

summary.en: Answer reviewers calmly, point by point, and see rejection as free advice.
summary.ur: Reviewers ko pur-sukoon, point by point jawab dein, aur radd hone ko muft mashwara samjhein.

back.en: One that takes fees but offers little or no real peer review and misleads authors.
back.ur: Jo fees leta hai lekin asal peer review kam ya bilkul nahi deta aur musannifon ko gumrah karta hai.

front.en: Where should you verify a journal's indexing?

back.en: In the database itself (PubMed, Scopus, DOAJ), not on the journal's website.
back.ur: Database mein khud (PubMed, Scopus, DOAJ), journal ki website par nahi.

back.en: A table answering each reviewer comment and showing where the paper changed.
back.ur: Aisi table jo har reviewer comment ka jawab de aur dikhaye paper mein kahan badla.

front.en: Is open access the same as predatory?
front.ur: Kya open access aur predatory ek hi hain?

back.en: No; many good journals are open access.
back.ur: Nahi; bohat se achhe journals open access hain.

note.ur: Ethics ke bayanat jo journals mangte hain.
